title: Redwood discovery - model selection - CalmWave Tech
next_steps: Send model performance matrix and per-token cost comparison (Redwood)
Share SOC2 and security pack + VPC deployment notes (Redwood)
Schedule a short benchmarking session with their sample prompts (SE + Liam)
Propose pilot scope and pricing for Dedicated 2-week trial (Commercial)
Customer to circulate internal stakeholders and confirm timeline for pilot decision (Aisha)
action_items: Daniel Ortiz: run perf/latency estimation for 8k vs 32k context models by Wed 2026-10-23
Maya Chen: send pricing sheet and Dedicated pilot template by Tue 2026-10-22
Liam Park: share 3 representative prompt flows and multilingual samples by Fri 2026-10-24
summary: Discovery call focused on model selection for CalmWave's multi-lingual customer-support assistant. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments, trade-offs for long context (8k vs 32k), open model choices (Llama/Redwood-verified, Mistral-like, Llama 3 variants), and tool-calling / external API integration. High priority items: security docs, pilot pricing, and a benchmarking run with customer prompts.
topics: Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, i've got Daniel from our solutions team, do you want to intro?
[00:08] Daniel Ortiz: yeah hi all, Daniel Ortiz, solution engineer — I'll focus on perf, latency, model trade-offs.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: hi, Aisha here, CTO at CalmWave. We run a multilingual support assistant, lots of short chats and some long context ticket histories.
[00:23] Liam Park: Liam, ML eng; i'll be hands-on for any benchmarks.
[00:27] Sofia Ramos: Sofia, product lead, mainly here to understand UX constraints and timeline.
[00:34] Maya Chen: great, quick agenda — 1) current stack and constraints 2) model selection (open models, context, tool-calling) 3) deployment options 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:44] Aisha Khan: yes. Quick note — security and data residency are important; SOC2 and SSO are musts.
[00:50] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll share our security pack.
[00:54] Liam Park: i'll give a quick overview of our workloads — mostly customer support: 60% short chats (<200 tokens), 30% multi-turn with context up to 6k tokens, 10% long thread summarization that can extend beyond 10k. Also need Spanish/Portuguese and occasional Japanese. Latency target is <600ms for short responses, and cost needs to be optimized — we're evaluating hosted for speed but open to Dedicated for cost control.
[01:22] Daniel Ortiz: thanks, that helps. Two quick clarifying q's: do you need tool-calling (like retrieving tickets/APIs) from the model, or is everything pure text generation?
[01:30] Liam Park: yes, we want tool-calling — the model should call our ticket API and also trigger structured responses for downstream systems.
[01:37] Maya Chen: perfect, Redwood supports function/tool-calling and structured outputs. For model selection — are you looking for highest quality single-turn answers, or multi-turn with long context preservation?
[01:46] Sofia Ramos: multi-turn consistency matters more. We need the assistant to maintain context across a 20-30 message thread and reference past user-provided attachments sometimes.
[01:55] Daniel Ortiz: okay, so context length requirement is real. We usually recommend considering 8k context models as minimum and 32k if you expect document-level context or attachments. For your 10k summarizations, 32k or an approach with KV caching + retrieval looks right.
[02:10] Aisha Khan: what's the cost delta between 8k and 32k models on hosted? Ballpark.
[02:16] Maya Chen: ballpark — depends on model and quantization. Roughly 2-3x token-cost for 32k compared to 8k for same throughput, but we can often use a hybrid: use shorter-context cheaper model for chat and route summarization to a higher-context model or use retrieval + chunked context.
[02:31] Liam Park: we prefer open models — are there Redwood-verified open checkpoints that support function-calling? And how good is multilingual out of the box?
[02:40] Daniel Ortiz: good q. We maintain a catalog of verified open models with performance profiles. Many open checkpoints (Llama 3 style variants, Mistral family, etc.) support function-calling layers in our runtime. Multilingual capability varies — Llama3-style and some Mistral variants handle Spanish/Portuguese well; Japanese can be trickier and sometimes needs finetune or translations. We can share a matrix with accuracy per language.
[03:02] Sofia Ramos: can you run a bench with our prompts and languages?
[03:06] Daniel Ortiz: yes — if you share representative prompts and sample threads, we can run latency and quality evals on hosted and on Dedicated nodes. We typically do a small pilot with your prompt set.
[03:16] Aisha Khan: about Dedicated vs Private: security-wise, Dedicated might be fine, but we have customers in EU that require data residency — can Redwood support a VPC/private deployment in our cloud region?
[03:27] Maya Chen: yes — we support Private deployments and VPC options. For EU residency we can provision Private in their region or discuss on-prem if needed. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and committed capacity which helps with predictable throughput and cost.
[03:42] Liam Park: ok and how about latency? Our SLAs want p95 <800ms for short replies.
[03:48] Daniel Ortiz: with Dedicated and optimized runtime, we can meet that for many models on medium batch sizes. Hosted can also hit that for smaller models; it depends on model size, quantization, and batching. We'll include expected p50/p95 numbers in the perf matrix.
[03:59] Sofia Ramos: curious about tool-calling safety — can Redwood sandbox the calls and provide audit logs?
[04:05] Maya Chen: yes we have tracing and per-request audit metadata, and you can route tool-calls through proxy for sandboxing. Our observability includes per-route tracing and token-level cost.
[04:16] Aisha Khan: good. A couple of technical things — are there recommended quantization profiles to reduce cost but maintain NLU quality, esp. for Spanish and Portuguese?
[04:25] Daniel Ortiz: we have quantization recommendations per model family. For many Llama-like variants, int8/4 quant works for many NLU tasks with small quality drop; for low-resource languages or complex tokenization you might want int8 + finetune or distillation. We'll include examples.
[04:40] Liam Park: what's Redwood's approach to KV cache and long-range context? Do you rely on chunking or do you keep full KV in memory?
[04:49] Daniel Ortiz: runtime keeps KV cache for active sessions; for very long histories we recommend hybrid — keep short-term KV in memory, and for older context use retrieval to rehydrate relevant chunks; that preserves latency while giving effective long-context behavior.
[05:02] Aisha Khan: do you support 32k context models in Hosted today?
[05:06] Maya Chen: yes, we support 32k context variants on Hosted and Dedicated, though availability depends on the model and region. For high-throughput 32k use cases dedicated nodes are better for cost efficiency.
[05:16] Sofia Ramos: what about model updates and rollouts, we need stable behavior during releases.
[05:21] Daniel Ortiz: our rollout tooling supports canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous versions on quality regressions. We also integrate evals against your prompt set so you can detect regressions before rollout.
[05:34] Liam Park: how do you handle embeddings and reranking? We use embeddings for semantic search and reranking of prior tickets.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Redwood supports embeddings; we can recommend model pairs (one for generation, one for embeddings) and also provide reranking endpoints. Embedding vectors and retention policies configurable to meet compliance.
[05:53] Aisha Khan: ok, hypothetically if we pick Hosted first to speed up, and move to Dedicated for scale — what's the migration path?
[06:01] Maya Chen: same API and config layer, so client-side code changes are minimal. We can help migrate model pins and rollout policies. You can start on Hosted and then request Dedicated capacity when you want committed throughput.
[06:12] Daniel Ortiz: practically, we'd run a small pilot on Hosted with your prompts, measure latency/cost, then propose a Dedicated node sizing to meet your p95 and throughput — usually a 2-week pilot.
[06:22] Sofia Ramos: timeline — we want a decision within 4 weeks. Can Redwood turn around benchmarks in that window?
[06:28] Daniel Ortiz: yes, if we get prompts and sample traffic patterns we'll have initial bench in ~4 business days and a pilot proposal within a week after that.
[06:37] Liam Park: about licenses — any model licensing constraints we should be aware of if we pick open checkpoints?
[06:43] Maya Chen: depends on model. Many open checkpoints are permissive but some have restrictions. We'll flag license type in the model matrix.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: and data retention — we need option to not persist user PII and to enable customer-managed keys.
[06:57] Maya Chen: we support customer KMS/HSM integrations in Private, and Dedicated can be configured with restricted retention — we have options to disable logging of PII tokens. We'll include security details.
[07:08] Sofia Ramos: for multilingual evaluation — we'll provide Spanish and Portuguese samples; Japanese is lower priority but would like a short sample.
[07:15] Liam Park: i'll compile that and send to Daniel.
[07:18] Daniel Ortiz: perfect. One more question — for tool-calling, do you need complex tool orchestration or just simple API calls and structured outputs?
[07:25] Liam Park: simple calls with structured JSON responses and a webhook to our backend — no complex orchestration yet.
[07:31] Daniel Ortiz: got it, that's straightforward. Our function-calling supports typed JSON outputs and sync webhooks; we can also add intermediate validation policies.
[07:41] Aisha Khan: can we enforce RBAC on who can trigger certain tools?
[07:45] Maya Chen: yes, RBAC and SSO provisioning available; we can map routes to roles.
[07:50] Sofia Ramos: are there prebuilt connectors to ticketing systems?
[07:54] Daniel Ortiz: we have sample connectors and docs for common systems; usually customers build light integrations but we can provide templates.
[08:02] Maya Chen: moving towards wrap-up — agreed action items: Liam will send prompts and language samples; Daniel will run bench and perf estimates; Maya will send pricing/security.
[08:13] Aisha Khan: sounds good. One more quick latency note — what batching strategy would you recommend for low-latency chat?
[08:20] Daniel Ortiz: we recommend aggressive small-batch optimization and dynamic batching; Dedicated gives better control over batching to meet p95. We'll include recommended batching config for chat vs summarization.
[08:32] Liam Park: for the summarization flows that go beyond 10k, would you suggest 32k model or retrieval + chunking?
[08:38] Daniel Ortiz: if you need true single-shot summarization of very long docs, 32k helps. If you can tolerate a multi-step pipeline, retrieval + chunked summarization with reranker is often more cost-efficient.
[08:50] Sofia Ramos: what's the expected RPS we can support per Dedicated pod?
[08:55] Daniel Ortiz: depends on model and GPU; we'll provide sample throughput numbers in the proposal. For instance, a mid-tier instance can handle X qps for small models and Y qps for 32k models — exacts in the doc.
[09:07] Aisha Khan: ok. can you give a quick example of how you'd route requests to cheaper models when possible?
[09:12] Maya Chen: yes — smart routing: short queries go to a cheaper, lower-context model; when ticket history or attachments are present we route to higher-context or retrieval-augmented flow. Policies are configurable and can fallback if capacity limits hit.
[09:29] Liam Park: any concerns about hallucination when calling tools?
[09:33] Daniel Ortiz: we mitigate with schema-enforced outputs, verification calls, and post-call validation. For critical actions we recommend two-step confirmations.
[09:43] Sofia Ramos: fine. timeline recap? we'll share prompts by Fri 2026-10-24, expect initial bench ~4 business days after that.
[09:52] Maya Chen: yes, and we'll send pricing + security docs by Tue 2026-10-22.
[09:58] Aisha Khan: thanks, appreciate it.
[10:00] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark slot.
[10:05] [meeting end]
